resources.string: Paste an SMS or WhatsApp message about Mobile Money. You can also share it directly to MoMo Shield.
Privacy: the analysis runs entirely on your phone. The app has no Internet access and does not read your SMS.
This analysis is a decision aid, not a guarantee. When in doubt, check with your operator’s official customer service.
No sign of a scam detected, but stay careful: no analysis is perfect.
This message shows suspicious signs. Do not reply, do not send money and check with an official source.
This message strongly looks like a scam. Do not click any link, do not give any code and do not send money.
No known scam sign was found in this message.
Artificial intelligence analysis (TensorFlow Lite): %1$d %% scam probability.
Artificial intelligence model unavailable: rules-only analysis.
A number in this message is in your list of reported numbers.
You are asked for your PIN, a password or a code received by SMS. An operator or a bank never asks for it.
Classic sent-by-mistake scam: you are pressured to send money back. First check your balance through the official menu.
The message presents you as the winner of a draw or a gift you never entered.
You are asked to pay to receive a prize, a loan, a parcel or a job. This is a typical sign of a scam.
The message announces a block or a suspension to push you to act without thinking.
The message claims to come from an operator but is sent from an ordinary number.
The author pretends to be an agent, customer service or a relative.
Asks you to contact a number
You are asked to call, write or send money to a number.
The message tries to make you act fast, without checking.
The message contains a link that does not lead to a known official site.
No check yet. Only the first 200 characters of each message are kept, on this phone only.
All saved checks will be deleted from this phone.
Add scammer numbers. MoMo Shield will warn you if they show up again in a message. The list stays on this phone.
Paste a message to check first.
The check failed. Please try again.
Neither your operator nor your bank will ask for your PIN, your password or a code received by SMS, whether by message, call or WhatsApp. Not even a so-called agent.
Sent by mistake: check before sending back

Fake confirmation messages are common. Before sending money back, check your real balance through your operator’s official menu. For a genuine error, the operator can handle the reversal: contact its official customer service.
A prize you never entered is a scam
If you did not take part in any draw, you won nothing. Nobody asks you to pay to receive a real prize.
Beware of shortened links and names that imitate an operator (mtn-momo-gain, orange-verif…). Always use the official website or app.
Within 24 hours, or your account will be blocked: scammers rush you so you cannot think. Take the time to check.
A relative with a new number
If a relative writes from a new number asking for money, call their old number or another family member before sending anything.
A real recruiter, scholarship or loan never asks for upfront fees through Mobile Money.

Contact your operator’s official customer service as soon as possible to try to block the transaction, keep the evidence (screenshots, numbers), change your PIN and report the facts to the authorities.
Add scammer numbers in the Reported tab: the app will warn you if they contact you again. Share these tips with your relatives.
Enable background analysis to be alerted instantly when receiving a suspicious SMS or message.
MoMoShield securely analyzes your messages in the background.
